title: Woman Watches a Krispy Kreme Customer Insult the Workers. Then the Situation Becomes Even More Uncomfortable - NewsBreak
text:
By Terrina Jairaj ,
1 hours ago Images by Sarah @sarah.chio on TikTok A woman’s recent video is making waves online after she shared an all-too-familiar story about a stranger who refused to take a hint. Sarah Chio, @sarah.chio on TikTok, known for her makeup, lifestyle, and new-mom content, posted a clip recounting a run-in with a Krispy Kreme customer who turned a simple donut run into an uncomfortable ordeal. The video has struck a chord with viewers, many who have dealt with situations where politeness is mistaken for an invitation to overstep.
Chio’s story begins innocently enough. She was at Krispy Kreme, picking up a banana bread donut, when an older woman decided to strike up a conversation. What started as small talk quickly spiraled into something far more awkward. The woman complained about the kids sitting nearby, muttering that “no one should have kids if you can’t handle them.”
Chio, a mom herself, kept her cool but couldn’t shake the feeling that the woman was looking for an argument. The interaction only got weirder from there. The woman fixated on Chio’s thrifted boots, asked where she got them, and launched into a rant about how “everything’s not the same anymore,” even dropping a few muttered curses for good measure.
Things took a turn when the woman got served first, despite Chio being next in line Instead of letting it go, she made a scene, huffing at the staff and insisting they’d “ignored” Chio. Chio, who admitted she’s not one to make a fuss, brushed it off – until the woman started hovering over her shoulder as she picked out her donuts. “She’s that type of woman,” Chio said, visibly uncomfortable. “Like, what are you doing, lady? Just go away.”
The final straw came when the woman berated a Krispy Kreme employee for not giving her a bag, calling her a “stupid, stupid girl” and demanding “serviettes” (a term most people haven’t used in ages). Chio, recounting the encounter, snapped saying. “Lady, you are the least important person in this entire establishment,” she said. “You need to chill out.”
@sarah.chio Gosh how do I always find myself in these interactions… #storytime #rant #krispykreme #cartalks #girltalk @Krispy Kreme
♬ original sound – Sarah Chio The video has resonated with viewers because it captures a frustrating dynamic many people recognize: the stranger who treats public spaces like their personal therapy session. Chio’s experience is about the broader expectation that people should always be “nice,” even when someone is clearly overstepping.
The woman in the story didn’t just ignore social cues; she doubled down, turning a mundane errand into a confrontation. For Chio, and for many who watched the video, the takeaway was simple: you don’t owe strangers your energy, and disengaging isn’t rude – it’s self-preservation.
The comments section lit up with people sharing their own experiences One user wrote, “She was trying to siphon your energy, girl. I know it can be awkward/hard, I struggle with it too and in the moment can tend to fawn when uncomfortable, but learning to ignore or say ‘sorry not interested’… I mean even for a stranger you don’t even owe them an explanation.”
Another, who works in customer service, added, “As soon as I get a cranky customer I’m still willing to do my job properly until they start insulting. It just annoys me how infuriating customers are over fast food.” The sentiment was clear: no one should have to endure rudeness just to avoid being seen as “cold.”
Chio’s video taps into a larger conversation about boundaries in casual interactions. In an era where people are more vocal about protecting their mental space, the idea that politeness requires endless patience for strangers feels outdated.
The COVID-19 pandemic shifted how many people view social interactions It is more acceptable to prioritize peace over forced small talk. Chio’s story is a perfect example of why that shift matters. Apart from being annoying, the woman at Krispy Kreme was draining. Chio implies that she was the kind of person who turns a quick stop into a psychological marathon. Chio’s minimal engagement, even when it felt awkward, was a small act of self-defense.
What makes the video so relatable is how it highlights the unspoken pressure to be “nice” at all costs. Chio admitted she felt awkward about shutting the woman down, even though she knew the interaction was unwanted. That hesitation is something many people, especially women, can relate to. Society often expects women to be accommodating, even when it comes at their own expense.
By the end of the video, she’s done. “Don’t be nice to everyone,” she says. “Mind your business. Cause you get wrapped up in conversations where people are trying to put negative energy on you.” The donut, by the way, was a little too heavy on the banana.
(Featured images: Sarah @sarah.chio on TikTok)
